main_text.p: tisui, albus videlicet spiritus vitrioli Veneris ex Marte, an universalis universalissimi, eruditorum facio judicii. Ex una enim radice tum astrum Solis & Mercurii, tum Mercurium & Sulphur Philosophorum provenire ait, primùm quidem spiritum album, quem diserte Mercurium Philosophorum vocat: postea enim sequitur spiritus rubeus (inquit) id est sulphur Philosophorum, & oleum incombustibile, puta ex utraq; tinctura Veneris & Martis in unum pariter coeuntium. Videantur quæ cap. de vitriolo apud eundem habentur pag. 132. quid illic de spiritu albo ad album & ad rubeum de rubeo analogicè Philosophetur Philosophus.
Apparet igitur rubeam mineram Cinnabaris Paracelsicæ & mineram

page.notes: The text is partly faint; underlining and italics are as seen. The word "quidem" and a few words in the upper lines are slightly blurred but read with reasonable confidence. The left-margin mark is a manuscript-like symbol and is not transcribed. The final line "neram" is set flush right and is transcribed as printed in the last line of the paragraph (the hyphenated word "mineram" is continued as "neram" at the line end).
